notes.note: Read Secs. 3, 5 (heuristics results) and 6. Review of 40 total tardiness methods: insertion and interchange heuristics (ENS1, ENS2 starting from NEHedd) best among heuristics; NEHedd outranks EDD; simulated annealing methods best metaheuristics; adapted makespan methods perform well for tardiness. 10.5267_j.ijiec.2017.2.001.title: Flow-shop scheduling problem under uncertainties: Review and trends
10.5267_j.ijiec.2017.2.001.venue: International Journal of Industrial Engineering Computations

notes.note: Read Secs 1, 3 (method, 3.1-3.3), 4. Systematic review of 100 FS/FFS papers 2001-2016 under uncertainty: processing times uncertain in 74%, probability distributions 57%, stochastic approach 60%; most papers optimize makespan alone; calls for tardiness and weighted criteria and uncertain release dates and weights.

Simheuristic (ILS plus Monte Carlo) for PFSP with stochastic times, expected makespan; lognormal Var=k*E, k=0.1 to 5 on Taillard instances; assumes good deterministic solutions are good stochastic ones at moderate variability; stochastic-deterministic gap 0.13% to 1.22%; argues for distributional (reliability) comparison beyond the mean; future work: criteria other than makespan.

10.1016_j.ejor.2003.08.027.matched_title: Executing production schedules in the face of uncertainties: A review and some future directions.

notes.note: Read abstract, Secs 1-4. Review of executing production schedules under disruptions: completely reactive, robust, predictive-reactive. Summarizing Lawrence and Sewell (1997) and Matsuura et al. (1993): optimization-based predictive schedules beat myopic dispatching under little uncertainty, but past a system-dependent variability level the advantage fades; right-shifting keeps the predictive schedule. Recommends reducing variability under high uncertainty.
